To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) parallel search is possible for unique items that are different in one feature, but (b) not when these items are different in two features.
search for a target that is defined by a unique form is slowed down by a unique-color distractor, and search for a target defined by a unique color is slowed down by an unique-form distractor.

(1) search for a unique color is not possible in a display with a salient form distractor, and search for a unique salient form is not possible when a salient color distractor is present, and (2) search for a salient form in a display with only a salient form is possible, and search for salient color in a display with salient color is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how attentional selection is guided.
the role of attention in perception.
the question of what happens when two or more stimuli compete for the attention of a single observer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the preattentively selected feature is the one that is most discriminable in the display.
the preattentively selected item in a visual search task can be a particular feature, but not a particular feature in a particular dimension.
the parallel search stage is selective only for a unique feature and not for a particular feature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preattentively guided search is not a unitary process but a process that is dependent on the stimulus characteristics.
parallel search can be guided to a particular feature, but only if the other features are not discriminable.
there are two types of visual selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the preattentively guided search stage, there is not only a selection of the target feature but also of the target dimension.
the visual search system does not have the capacity to completely select for a particular target feature.
the preattentively guided attentional spotlight is not completely flexible.
